license: Original code and fixtures authored for this evaluation. No upstream source file is copied into this package. The defect pattern that environment/workspace/wsparse reproduces is documented upstream: CPython issue 39910, "os.ftruncate on Windows should be sparse" (reporter Mingye Wang, filed 2020-03-09, status open), whose reproduction is `os.truncate('1.txt', 1024 ** 3)` followed by `fsutil sparse queryFlag 1.txt`, and whose recommended fix is to issue FSCTL_SET_SPARSE before extending the file, as aria2 does in src/AbstractDiskWriter.cc.
lineage: Public upstream defect report (CPython issue 39910: truncating/extending a file on Windows allocates every cluster, while the Unix behaviour is sparse) -> workspace module wsparse frozen in that defective shape -> Windows/NTFS sparse-file contract expressed as acceptance criteria A-G -> evaluator-side independent measurement through fsutil and Win32 queries on its own handle -> local oracle/no-change differential calibration -> container control runs on the pinned Windows Server Core image.
pollution_risk: Low. The subject is NTFS sparse-file allocation semantics driven through DeviceIoControl (FSCTL_SET_SPARSE, FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES, FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA) plus the physical-size queries GetCompressedFileSizeW and FILE_STANDARD_INFO.AllocationSize. A dedup sweep over all 158 records of the procurement Base for the keywords sparse / 稀疏 / prealloc / 预分配 / ftruncate / truncate / 磁盘占用 / 物理大小 / GetCompressedFileSize / allocated range / 压缩属性 / FSCTL returned only four hits, none of which is an NTFS sparse-file task (they are win-cpython-zip-path-containment, wchunk-216, wfmt-215 and wlogseg-218, all about containers, zip path containment and log segmentation). No other task in this batch depends on cluster-allocation metadata, so a relabelled duplicate is not possible. No sample file is shared with any other task: the workspace ships a single generated dense control file, and every sparse fixture is created by the evaluator on its own handle.
authorization: No external repository is vendored. The only third-party artefacts are the pinned Microsoft Windows Server Core base image, the PSF-licensed Python 3.12.9 embeddable distribution, MinGit and the offline wheelhouse already used by the other tasks in this batch. No network access is required to build or grade the task.
